parties: Astron Paper & Board Mill Limited (debtor company); NCLT; insolvency professional (appointed)
headline: Astron Paper & Board Mill Limited enters Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Astron Paper & Board Mill Limited has been admitted to Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), as notified to NSE; the company is now under the supervision of an insolvency professional and subject to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
implication: Creditors and stakeholders must file claims within the statutory window; NCLT jurisdiction and the 180-day (extendable to 270-day) resolution timeline governs the process; any M&A, asset sales or reorganisation will be subject to the Committee of Creditors' approval under IBC protocol.
detail: Astron Paper & Board Mill Limited has informed the NSE of entry into CIRP, triggering mandatory disclosures under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and NCLT Rules. The company is now under NCLT supervision with an insolvency professional appointed as interim resolution professional. Creditors must lodge claims within the prescribed statutory period. The resolution plan, if any, must be approved by the Committee of Creditors and thereafter by NCLT, or the company will proceed to liquidation.

central; resolution professional powers, prohibition on transactions during moratorium, resolution plan approval

framework.ref: NCLT (Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process) Rules, 2016, r. 13
framework.note: central; resolution plan criteria and approval threshold (75% of voting share of CoC)

central; creditors other than financial creditors (operational creditors) claim procedures

conditions: Admission of company to CIRP by NCLT
Declaration of moratorium under IBC §14 preventing new legal proceedings and asset disposal
Constitution of Committee of Creditors (within 7 days of admission)
Creditors to file claims within statutory period (typically 14 days of newspaper publication)
Resolution plan to be developed and voted on by CoC (requiring 75% approval by voting share)
NCLT approval of final resolution plan or declaration of failure and liquidation
approvals: Committee of Creditors resolution plan approval (≥75%)

triggers.note: CIRP initiated by application of financial creditor, operational creditor, or debtor; triggers mandatory admission if documentary evidence of default/insolvency present
Listed company must notify stock exchange of CIRP admission as material event affecting the company
Upon CIRP admission, automatic moratorium on all legal proceedings, recoveries, and asset disposals (subject to exceptions)
